title: Dynamic function contract compiler and cross-SDK invocation adapter
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Developers using our SDKs (Python/TS/Go) need consistent and ergonomic function/tool-calling behavior across languages. Current SDKs have subtle differences in schema validation, retry semantics, and streaming invocation ergonomics which leads to customer bugs and longer onboarding. Goal: Build a small "contract compiler" that turns a canonical function signature into language-specific runtime validators and a lightweight invocation adapter that plugs into each SDK runtime. The adapter will provide: (1) strong runtime validation (JSON Schema derived from canonical contract), (2) standardized retry/backoff semantics with idempotency handling and automatic resumable streaming where supported, (3) telemetry hooks for per-call validation failures and retry cost, and (4) migration/compatibility modes to support existing apps.
acceptance_criteria: A: Canonical contract -> JSON Schema pipeline implemented and tested in a standalone repo
B: Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs include generated validators and use the same validation semantics by default
C: Invocation adapter exposes a single ergonomic call wrapper that supports sync/async, streaming chunks, and explicit resume tokens
D: Retry behavior matches the SDK policy doc (idempotency-aware, exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts configurable) and is observable via telemetry
E: End-to-end integration tests against the hosted API that exercise validation errors, retry loops, and streaming resume paths
F: Migration guide and example apps updated with patterns and anti-patterns
G: Performance overhead of validation and adapter is <5% P50 latency compared to baseline caller in perf harness
H: Security review completed and SCA of codegen tool performed
technical_notes: Design: keep a single canonical function contract format (subset of OpenAPI + extended metadata) and generate a JSON Schema as the portable validator artifact.

Codegen: codegen emits small runtime validator bundles for each language (Python: pydantic-lite + fast checks; TS: zod schema; Go: generated struct tags + runtime checks). These bundles are embedded in SDK releases or downloadable at runtime for dynamic contracts.

Streaming: adapter will convert token/stream chunks into a typed chunk event with optional resume token. Resume tokens are opaque UUIDs backed by the service's KV cache; adapter can retry from resume token when supported.
Retries: adapter consults contract metadata for idempotency and side-effect hints. Non-idempotent calls default to fewer retry attempts unless explicitly opted-in via call options.
Telemetry: events emitted for validation failures, retry attempts, final call success/failure, and streaming resumes. Tagging includes model, contract key, sdk-language, and route.
Compatibility: provide a compatibility flag 'legacy_validation: true' to use the previous permissive behavior for customers needing gradual migration.
Security: generated validators run sandboxed (no dynamic exec where avoidable). All codegen outputs pass SCA and linter gates in CI.
Observability: expose per-invocation trace IDs so Console can join SDK validation and server-side traces for end-to-end debugging.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed. Prototype contract -> JSON Schema converter (Go) and small TS validator using zod. Found early mismatch with optional vs nullable semantics across languages.
2026-02-28: Prototype demo to SDK-Eng: validated that resume-token model requires a stable KV key format; outlined a token TTL strategy with ops.
2026-03-03: Implemented initial adapter API shape in Python and TS: call_with_contract(contract, input, options) -> supports streaming generator and resume option. Local smoke tests pass.
2026-03-05: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/compare/PR-4123 (codegen + TS adapter). Initial review by @emily. Waiting on Go codegen scaffolding.
2026-03-09: Added telemetry hooks and test harness for measuring retry amplification. Observed 12% cost increase in pathological retry test; added circuit-breaker guard to limit amplification.
2026-03-10: Design review with PM and Security. Security requested SCA and deterministic codegen outputs for reproducible builds. Assigned follow-up items.
review_feedback: From PM (Jon Patel): ensure migration path is simple; add CLI to generate validator bundles for customers who want to precompile validators in CI.
From Design (Clara Nguyen): make the streaming resume UX explicit in examples—show two patterns (automatic resume vs manual token handoff).
From Security (Priya Menon): disallow arbitrary code execution during codegen; require deterministic hashes and sign bundles uploaded to artifact registry.
From SDK lead (Ravi Singh): prefer zod/pydantic equivalents rather than introducing a new validator runtime. Keep bundles < 30KB when possible.
qa_plan: Unit tests for contract compiler: edge cases for nested optional/nullable, enums, and arrays
Language-specific validator unit tests (Python/TS/Go) exercising success and failure paths
Integration tests against staging inference endpoints: validation-reject scenarios, retry loops with simulated transient errors, streaming resume with forced mid-stream failure
Performance regression tests in perf harness (compare baseline caller vs adapter enabled)
Fuzz tests for resume tokens and schema mismatch handling
Security checks: SCA, reproducible build verification, and static analysis of codegen outputs
examples: examples/function-call-examples/python-contractor: example app showing generator-based streaming resume and explicit resume token flow
examples/function-call-examples/ts-atomic-invoker: TS example with zod validators and automatic retry wrapper
examples/function-call-examples/go-safe-invoker: Go example demonstrating precompiled validators and graceful backoff handling
notes: Follow-up: coordinate with runtime team for stable resume token semantics (OPS ticket expected)
Consider publishing validator bundles to CDN for hosted customers to reduce client-side warmup time
Keep generator/async streaming behavior consistent between SDKs; map to idiomatic language constructs (async iterator in TS/Python, channel-based stream in Go).
